findings.title: MetricAlertDetectorHandler is now abstract and cannot be instantiated.
findings.body:
`MetricAlertDetectorHandler` now subclasses `StatefulDetectorHandler` with just `pass`. That leaves the abstract methods unimplemented: `get_dedupe_value`, `get_group_key_values` and the new `build_occurrence_and_event_data`. Before this change, the handler had a stub `evaluate` that returned `[]`, so it was safe to run.

`MetricAlertFire` appears to register this class as its `detector_handler`; that part is not shown in the hunk. If it does, `Detector.detector_handler` will raise `TypeError: Can't instantiate abstract class` for any metric-alert detector. `process_detectors` would then crash for every data packet that reaches such a detector, instead of skipping it.

Fix: keep a non-abstract stub until the stateful implementation exists. For example, implement the three abstract methods with placeholder bodies (`return 0`, `return {}`, `raise NotImplementedError` behind a guard), or keep subclassing `DetectorHandler` with an `evaluate` that returns `{}`.

findings.title: The expected occurrence uses group key "val1" but the result being checked is for "group_key".
findings.body: In `TestEvaluateGroupKeyValue.test_dedupe`, the expected result has `group_key="group_key"` and `evaluate_group_key_value` is called with that key. But the occurrence is built for `"val1"`, so its fingerprint is `["<id>:val1"]` while the handler produces `["<id>:group_key"]`. `IssueOccurrence` is a dataclass and compares by fields, so any assertion that the returned result equals `expected_result` will fail. I can't see the rest of this test, so I couldn't confirm that such an assertion exists. Build the occurrence with `expected_result.group_key` (or `"group_key"`) and the value 10 that the test actually passes in.

findings.title: The `evaluate` docstring still says it returns a list.
findings.body: The signature now returns `dict[DetectorGroupKey, DetectorEvaluationResult]`, but the unchanged docstring right below it still says "returns a list of `DetectorEvaluationResult`". Update it to say the method returns a dict keyed by group key.

findings.title: The expected values don't match the test data: group_2 is 10 but the expected occurrence uses 6.
findings.body: The packet sets `"group_2": 10`, but the expected occurrence for group_2 is built with value 6. The same thing happens in `test_results_on_change` (input 100) and `TestEvaluate.test_dedupe` (input 8). These tests only pass because the mock builder ignores `value`. Once a real builder uses `value`, they will check the wrong thing. Pass the actual input value.
